parsed_artifact.adjudication_notes: The finding correctly identifies that top-degree vanishing arguments via Steinberg module coinvariants require proving that the Mod-orbit of the hyperelliptic Steinberg image generates all of St_g. This is a nontrivial requirement that cannot be bypassed by fixed-point arguments or by invoking transitivity on geometric objects (curves, chains, simplices) that are not Steinberg generators. The Broaddus reference is appropriate. The finding should be promoted from candidate to corroborated as it identifies a legitimate technical obstruction in the literature.
parsed_artifact.contradiction_resolution: No contradictions with cross-checked claims. Compatible with FND-0035 (vcd formula), FND-0018/FND-0024 (top-degree vanishing structure), and the general framework of mapping class group cohomology. The finding identifies a genuine technical gap in arguments that attempt to use hyperelliptic involutions to force S^-=0 without proving the stronger generation statement.

mathematical_verification.broaddus_reference: Legitimate: Broaddus (arXiv:0909.2901) studies generation of the Steinberg module and identifies specific cyclic generators; the finding correctly references this work
mathematical_verification.generation_requirement: Correct: To prove (St⊗V)_{Mod}=0 for odd Sp-inflated V, one needs the Mod-orbit of im(b) to generate St_g as a Mod-module, not merely that a hyperelliptic involution fixes certain chains
mathematical_verification.hyperelliptic_map: Correct: Birman-Hilden theory gives a map from Mod(Σ_{0,2g+2}) to the hyperelliptic subgroup of Mod_g, inducing b: St(Σ_{0,2g+2}) → St_g on Steinberg modules
mathematical_verification.invalid_shortcuts: Correct: (1) Maximal simplices in the curve complex are not Steinberg generators; (2) Humphries generators give Dehn twists, not Steinberg module generators; (3) Mod-transitivity on filling curves does not imply transitivity on Steinberg generators
mathematical_verification.steinberg_duality: Correct: Virtual duality groups satisfy H^{vcd}(G;V) ≅ (St⊗V)_G where St is the dualizing module; for Mod_g this is the Steinberg module from the curve complex
mathematical_verification.vcd_formula: Correct: vcd(Mod_g) = 4g-5 for g>=2 with n=0, confirmed by Harer and packet FND-0023

scope.applies_to: top-degree vanishing arguments using Steinberg module coinvariants H^{4g-5}(Mod_g;V) ≅ (St⊗V)_{Mod}
scope.generality: all g >= 2 where virtual duality and Steinberg module theory apply
